sanity_expectations: R is finite, real and non-negative across the sampled region
R increases monotonically with h2 at fixed S, t_gen
R rises with S at small S then saturates/bends (Gaussian variance-depletion and Michaelis-type finite-variance factors)
R decreases with increasing t_gen toward a plateau (erosion factor)
At large S the environmental-gain factor lifts R by up to gamma_env (~40%) relative to the parent equation
excitation_report: sigma=0.01, k=5. Dominant (whole multiplicative) term: RMS 0.307 -> 30.7x sigma. NEW term (environmental-variance gain factor 1 + gamma_env*S^2/(S_env^2+S^2), i.e. E - parent): max_effect 0.127 -> 12.7x sigma, strongest at h2~0.83, S~2.30, t_gen~2.24 (interior of sampled box). No weak terms; all terms visible above noise.
role_corrections: R: output->dependent variable (confirmed; LHS, explicitly solvable)
h2: input/time-axis->independent variable (confirmed as sampling axis; heritability, not literally time)
S: input/time-axis->independent variable (confirmed as sampling axis)
t_gen: input/time-axis->independent variable (confirmed; generation count is the nearest-to-time axis)
rationale: Purely algebraic explicit relation R = f(h2, S, t_gen; params) with no derivatives or integrals (analyze_expression: max_derivative_order 0, no kernels, explicitly_solvable_for_target). Three independent sampling axes h2 (heritability, 0.05-0.9), S (selection differential, 0.1-4 phenotypic SD) and t_gen (generations, 0-20); the eight remaining symbols are fixed physical constants at biologically sensible magnitudes. gamma_env=0.4 and S_env=1.5 (within the suggested 0-0.5 and 0.5-4.0) make the new environmental-variance-reduction factor clearly visible (12.7x sigma) without unphysical values. check_substitution at a representative interior point returns finite real R=0.404.

scenario_text: A quantitative trait is influenced by many additive genetic loci plus environmental variation, and offspring resemble their parents according to the additive genetic contribution. The expected shift in the offspring mean after selecting parents depends on the proportion of trait variance that is heritable and the strength of the applied selection. Breeders record the response to selection across trials with varying heritability and selection differential. Dominance and epistasis are treated as absent.
